subject.title: [Feature]: Allow job-level model override for cron jobs using sessionTarget=main + payload.kind=systemEvent

question: Should main-session `systemEvent` cron jobs gain a supported model/provider override contract, and if so should that contract be `payload.model`, job-level fields, or an explicit session override shape?
rationale: This changes the public cron schema, model/provider precedence, persisted payload behavior, and main-session state semantics, so source inspection can prove the gap but cannot choose the long-term API contract.

options.title: Extend systemEvent payload.model
options.body: Add `payload.model` to systemEvent as the narrowest contract matching agentTurn, with allowlist validation and run-scoped session override behavior.

options.title: Add a broader job override shape
options.body: Introduce job-level `model`/`provider` or a `sessionOverride` object so multiple payload kinds can share one explicit override model at the cost of a larger schema surface.

options.title: Keep main systemEvent text-only
options.body: Leave main-session systemEvent jobs on the session default and document isolated agentTurn jobs as the supported model-controlled cron path.

recommendation.title: Extend systemEvent payload.model
recommendation.body: Add `payload.model` to systemEvent as the narrowest contract matching agentTurn, with allowlist validation and run-scoped session override behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available routing signal is prior work around cron session-target and model-routing behavior, though the local import-heavy history makes ownership only medium-confidence.
